title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: S over T, and E an abelian sheaf (in practice a quasi-coherent module or vector group) on S with a stratification of infinite order relative to T. The stratification is encoded by a homomorphism δ = δ^∞_E : E → P^∞_{S/T}(E) into the sheaf of infinite-order principal parts (jets). P^∞_{S/T}(E) carries its canonical stratification, and δ is a map of stratified sheaves. The universal Taylor map is d^∞_{S/T} : E → P^∞_{S/T}(E). We have an exact sequence 0 → E → P^∞(E) → P^∞(E)/δE → 0 (eq. (2') on the previous page).

Goal: describe a stratification on an E-torsor P that is compatible with the stratification of E. This is the torsor analogue of the module case. It is preparation for §3 on the next page: the associated integrable connection d^0_P : P → E⊗Ω^1, and eventually Gauss–Manin for affine torsors.

Argument, partly on the previous page.
- A stratified E-torsor is the same thing as a stratified P^∞(E)-torsor together with a trivialisation of its pushout along p : P^∞(E) → P^∞(E)/δE, the trivialisation being compatible with stratifications.
- Stratified P^∞(E)-torsors are the same as ordinary E-torsors P. The correspondence is P ↦ P^∞_{S/T}(P), the jets of P.
- A trivialisation of the pushout P^∞(P)/δE amounts to a sheaf map λ : P → P^∞(E)/δE (26) satisfying the equivariance condition λ(x+ξ) = λ(x) + p(d^∞_{S/T}ξ) (27). Grothendieck corrected his first attempt, which lacked the p.
- Concretely, if the stratification of P is given by δ_P : P → P^∞(P), then λ(x) = class of (d^∞x − δ_P x). Indeed λ(x+ξ) − λ(x) = d^∞ξ − δξ, which is ≡ d^∞ξ mod δE.
- Compatibility with stratifications: since P is the sheaf of horizontal sections of P^∞(P) (horizontal sections of a jet sheaf recover the original sheaf), compatibility amounts to (28): λ(P) ⊂ (P^∞(E)/δE)^♮, where ♮ denotes the subsheaf of horizontal sections. The margin note says ♮ means taking homs from P^∞(P) into an arbitrary stratified torsor.

Summary (boxed with double bar): stratifications on the E-torsor P compatible with δ correspond to maps λ : P → (P^∞(E)/δE)^♮ (26') satisfying (27). The description is functorial in E and compatible with base change.

The next page rewrites λ via the splitting P^∞(E)^+ ≅ P^∞(E)/δE as λ^+ with λ^+(x+ξ) = λ^+(x) + d^+(ξ), where d^+ = d^∞ − δ. From this it extracts the connection d^0_P : P → E⊗Ω^1. Mathematically this is the standard non-abelian-free (affine torsor) version of 'a stratification is a Taylor-type map into jets', applied to torsors.
errors: The boxed summary says 'une stratification sur E rel. à T, compatible avec la stratification δ donnée sur E'. The first E should be P: the stratification is on the torsor P. This is a slip of the pen, or a misreading of the hand.
The notation for the quotient is inconsistent: '/δE' in (26) and (26'), but '/E' or '//E' in (28) and in the line 'P^∞(E)//E-torseurs'. All of these mean P^∞(E)/δ(E).
The map in (26) is first labelled λ_* (or λ_#, overwritten) and then simply λ.
The previous page's references '(cf. [ ])' are left blank; the canonical stratification of P^∞ and the fact that the horizontal sections of P^∞(P) are P are used without proof. Both are standard.

The margin explanation of ♮ ('hom de P^∞(P) dans un torseur stratifié quelconque') is vague. Taken literally as an adjunction it is not the usual one: P^∞ is right adjoint to the forgetful functor, not left. So it should be read as a heuristic remark, not a precise statement.

ideas.what: A stratified torsor under a stratified abelian sheaf E corresponds to an ordinary E-torsor P plus a map λ : P → P^∞(E)/δE that is affine over the Taylor map d^∞ (condition (27)) and lands in horizontal sections (condition (28)).
ideas.modern_name: Torsors under crystals / stratified (D-module) torsors; description of H^1 of a stratified sheaf via the jet resolution
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes, 1968); Berthelot (crystalline cohomology, 1974); Mazur–Messing (1974) for torsors with integrable connection under vector groups
ideas.where_published: Closest published material: 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968) and 'Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (1974). This exact torsor formulation: unsure.

ideas.what: The exact sequence 0 → E → P^∞(E) → P^∞(E)/δE → 0 of stratified sheaves, used to reduce E-torsors to P^∞(E)-torsors plus a trivialisation.
ideas.modern_name: Coinduced (jet) resolution; the infinite-order Spencer / de Rham resolution
ideas.where_published: EGA IV 16 (principal parts P^∞); Crystals and de Rham cohomology (1968)

ideas.what: Horizontal sections of the jet sheaf P^∞(P), with its canonical stratification, recover P.
ideas.modern_name: Horizontal sections of an induced / coinduced D-module

missed.claim: This page belongs to an unpublished, carefully structured treatment of stratifications and connections on affine torsors, meant to feed into a Gauss–Manin / Picard–Fuchs text. The bibliographic references are left blank, and the integrability conditions for the + -sections are only planned in the margin of the next page. It appears never to have been written up by Grothendieck himself in this form. Mathematically, however, it is standard.
missed.quote: Cette description est fonctorielle en E, et compatible aux changements de base.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly of historical interest. It documents Grothendieck's jet-theoretic approach to torsors with connection, contemporaneous with Mazur–Messing's universal vector extensions. No new mathematics for specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but routine translation of 'compatible stratification on an E-torsor' into jet-theoretic data. It contains no result beyond what crystalline and D-module theory of the period (Grothendieck 1968, Berthelot, Mazur–Messing) makes standard.
transcription_corrections: (26): the arrow label is a struck-through λ_# or λ_* corrected to λ; the target is P^∞_{S/T}(E)/δE.
Line after (27): 'P^∞_{S/T}(E)/δE - torseurs obtenus'. The '//E' in the transcription is the quotient by δE.
(28): the image reads (P^∞_{S/T}(E)/E)^♮. The superscript symbol is a hand-drawn sign for 'horizontal sections'; the next page's margin renders it as ♭.
Boxed summary: 'une stratification sur E rel. à T' — the hand seems to read E, but P is meant.
'(26) bis' is written as '(26' or '(26 bis' before 'les' / '(26')'.
The margin note reads approximately: 'le signe ♮ signifie prendre les hom de P^∞_{S/T}(P) dans un torseur stratifié quelc.' The struck word 'désigne' is replaced.
